---
title: "Aquaculture Resilience Evidence Engine (AREE)"
---

AREE is an open, reproducible research resource that converts fragmented public
omics datasets into **harmonized, comparable resilience-biomarker evidence** for
Pacific oyster (*Crassostrea gigas*) and, by design, other shellfish and
aquaculture organisms.

It is not a static resource list or a generic website. It is a versioned
evidence-generation system with five connected layers:

1. **Study registry & intake** — machine-readable registration of public
   datasets with controlled vocabularies for phenotypes and stressors.
2. **Standardized reanalysis workflows** — Nextflow workflows for RNA-seq,
   methylation, proteomics, and metabolomics (raw-reanalysis or
   processed-results modes).
3. **Cross-study harmonization** — a shared evidence schema plus identifier
   mapping with explicit confidence levels.
4. **Meta-analysis & candidate prioritization** — random-effects pooling,
   heterogeneity statistics, and a transparent (non-black-box) candidate score
   with hard tier gates.
5. **User-facing outputs** — this documentation site plus a Streamlit interface
   and downloadable evidence cards.

## Core principles

- **Association, not proof.** AREE surfaces evidence convergence, never confirmed
  mechanistic causation. A statistically significant hit in one study is never
  presented as a validated biomarker.
- **Provenance always.** Every result traces back to a source file, checksum,
  parameter set, and workflow version.
- **Missingness is explicit.** Missing metadata is recorded and reportable,
  never silently dropped or imputed.
- **Contradictions are surfaced.** Conflicting cross-study findings appear in
  meta-analysis summaries and evidence cards rather than being averaged away.

## Where to go next

- New here? Read [Why this resource matters](why_it_matters.md) and
  [Installation](installation.md).
- Want to add a dataset? See [Adding a study](adding_a_study.md).
- Curious how it works? See the [Technical architecture](architecture.md) and
  the [Design document](design.md).

> **Note on demo data.** Every demo dataset is labeled **simulated** and is
> partitioned from real evidence during pooling, ranking, and reporting. The
> repository also includes registered real public studies; do not cite a demo
> result as real biological evidence.
